## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from Springer publisher pages and domain knowledge of CBT research editorial culture (ABCT / EABCT). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Cognitive-behavioral therapy research — Beck's cognitive model, CBT outcome, cognitive processes in psychopathology, third-wave CBT (ACT, DBT, MBCT), mechanism-of-change |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **cognitive / behavioral therapy contribution** — outcome, process, mechanism, or theoretical advance in CBT framework.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Non-CBT clinical work redirected to JCCP or J Psychopathology.

Reviewers from CBT research community — ABCT (Association for Behavioral and Cognitive Therapies), EABCT international networks. Common demands: "Mechanism specification?", "CBT theoretical fidelity?", "Clinical significance?".

| **Dominant tradition** | CBT research — Springer flagship |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Non-CBT clinical work
- AI use without disclosure per Springer policy
- Insufficient mechanism / theoretical specification

### Soft Tax

Low for CBT research tradition authors.

### Best Suited For

- CBT outcome trials
- Cognitive mechanism research in anxiety / depression / OCD / PTSD
- Third-wave CBT empirical work (ACT, DBT, MBCT)
- Mechanism-of-change studies
- CBT meta-analyses
- Theoretical CBT contributions with empirical test

### Not Recommended For

- Non-CBT psychotherapy (consider JCCP)
- Pure psychopathology mechanism without therapy (consider J Psychopathology)
- Pure qualitative work
- Pure cognitive psychology

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology](./journal-of-consulting-and-clinical-psychology.md) | APA flagship for broader treatment outcome |
| 2 | [Clinical Psychology Review](./clinical-psychology-review.md) | If reframed as systematic review; Elsevier |
| 3 | [Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science](./journal-of-psychopathology-and-clinical-science.md) | If mechanism-focused without therapy |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JCCP as "too CBT-specific," CTR is the Springer ABCT-affiliated home for CBT research.
